Document applicant: "Endress+Hauser SE+Co. KG"

The difference: register says "GmbH + Co., KG" but document says "SE+Co. KG". GmbH vs SE is not just legal-suffix drift — GmbH (Gesellschaft mit beschränkter Haftung) and SE (Societas Europaea) are genuinely different legal entity forms. Endress+Hauser changed its legal form: Endress+Hauser GmbH+Co. KG became Endress+Hauser SE+Co. KG in 2014 (actually the company converted from GmbH+Co. KG to SE+Co. KG). Hmm, this is a real-world company: Endress+Hauser SE+Co. KG is the German sales company. So this could be a legal form change over time.

But the rules: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

Is GmbH vs SE "legal-suffix drift"? Legal-suffix drift typically refers to e.g. "GmbH" vs "GmbH & Co. KG" formatting, "Ltd" vs "Limited", punctuation/spacing differences. But GmbH → SE is a substantive change of legal form — SE is a European Company (Societas Europaea), a different corporate form. However, it's still the same company legally (continuation after change of legal form). But per the rules, the decision axis: are these the same entity?
